title: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society
measurement_description: The text is a comprehensive textbook on AI Safety, Ethics, and Society. It does not empirically measure or evaluate language models on faith or religion. Instead, it discusses religion theoretically in its 'Normative Ethics' chapter, exploring Divine Command Theory and the philosophical relationship between God and morality. It also briefly mentions religion as a legally protected class in the context of algorithmic fairness and bias.
findings: Conceptually, the text argues against equating religion with morality (highlighting the philosophical flaws of Divine Command Theory) while clarifying that this is not an argument against religion itself. It also establishes that AI systems must be designed to avoid discrimination based on legally protected attributes, which includes religion. There are no empirical findings related to LLM performance on religious tasks.
